about: Four verbs over the gifts, and the shortest prayer of the Canon. This is the place where the Roman Church inserted blessings of things brought up — oil, the fruits of the earth. The Pontifical still sets the blessing of the oil of the sick here, in the Maundy Thursday Mass. Hence hæc ómnia … bona creas: it speaks first of the things God creates — the Eucharistic gifts are not excluded from it. The relative quem reaches back to Christ, named at the end of the prayer before.

s01.translation: Through whom You continue to make all these good things, O Lord;

s02.narrative: Three signs of the cross over the Host and chalice together.

s03.translation: You sanctify them, fill them with life, bless them, and bestow them upon us.

w002.function: The relative reaches back to the Christ of the last words of Nobis quoque — that prayer has no Amen of its own and runs on into this one.

w007.function: Predicative with “creas” (w008): thou createst them good, not thou createst good things.
